hook: Chris Olah helped invent the field of mechanistic interpretability, the effort to reverse engineer the internal workings of neural networks into algorithms a person can actually read. He built that career without a college degree, funding it instead with a Thiel Fellowship, then spent years at Google Brain visualizing what neural networks see before leading interpretability research at OpenAI. In 2021 he co-founded Anthropic and now leads its interpretability work, publishing the Transformer Circuits research thread that tries to map language models circuit by circuit. He also co-founded Distill, a journal built around explaining machine learning clearly rather than tersely. In 2026 he took that argument to the Vatican, telling an audience beside Pope Leo XIV that AI's governance problems cannot be left to computer scientists alone.
name: Chris Olah

quote.text: No matter how sincerely any of us intend to do the right thing, and I believe many of us do, we will always be influenced by those incentives.
quote.context: From remarks Olah gave alongside Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican in May 2026, reported by Fortune.

primary.name: Anthropic, A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits

timeline.event: Awarded a Thiel Fellowship and forgoes a traditional undergraduate degree
timeline.impact: Chooses independent research over university study

timeline.event: Interns at Google Brain, hosted first by Jeff Dean and then by Greg Corrado
timeline.impact: Begins working on neural network interpretability and visualization

timeline.event: Serves as second author on Google's DeepDream visualization research
timeline.impact: Helps popularize techniques for seeing what neural networks respond to internally

timeline.event: Becomes a Research Scientist at Google Brain and co-founds the Distill journal
timeline.impact: Establishes a venue for rigorous, visual machine learning explanations

timeline.event: Joins OpenAI as a Member of Technical Staff, leading interpretability work
timeline.impact: Builds and leads the Clarity interpretability team
Helps start a public benefit corporation focused on AI safety and becomes head of its interpretability research

timeline.event: Publishes A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits with Anthropic colleagues
timeline.impact: Launches the Transformer Circuits research thread aimed at reverse engineering language models

timeline.event: Speaks alongside Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican following the Pope's encyclical on AI
timeline.impact: Argues publicly that AI governance cannot be left to technologists alone

quick_facts: Co-founder of Anthropic and its head of interpretability research
Previously led the interpretability (Clarity) team at OpenAI, and was a researcher at Google Brain
Co-founded Distill, a journal for clear, visual explanations of machine learning research
Awarded a Thiel Fellowship in 2012 and never completed a traditional undergraduate degree
Second author on Google's 2015 DeepDream neural network visualization work

achievements.title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits, 2021
achievements.impact: Led the founding paper of Anthropic's Circuits interpretability research thread, aiming to reverse engineer transformer language models into human understandable algorithms.

achievements.title: Co-founder, Distill
achievements.impact: Helped launch a journal for interactive, visually rigorous machine learning explanations, publishing widely read pieces such as Understanding LSTM Networks and The Building Blocks of Interpretability.

achievements.title: DeepDream visualization, 2015
achievements.impact: Served as second author on Google's widely known neural network visualization project.

achievements.title: Vatican address, 2026
achievements.impact: Invited to speak alongside Pope Leo XIV following the Pope's first encyclical addressing AI risk, arguing AI governance cannot be left to computer scientists alone.
